subject: Client handshake metadata gap - Novatech POC
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ashley Nguyen <ashley.novatech@novatech.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Client handshake metadata gap - Novatech POC

Hi team,

Quick summary: Novatech is seeing sessions where their per-call client metadata (x-client-id / x-call-meta) is not carried across a runtime-level reconnect/fallback. Symptoms: generation continues but telemetry shows the route_id changes and the incoming request on the fallback worker lacks the client metadata that the SDK originally sent. Customer impact: personalization keys in the prompt are missing for a subset of requests (~1.3% of calls during burst windows) which leads to incorrect answers and a noticeable drop in quality for their PoC.

What I have so far (attached): novatech-logs-20271101.txt contains two representative traces. The pattern appears when the runtime re-routes a streaming handshake to a fallback model during transient capacity pressure: the new session's headers are missing the x-client-id fields.

Ask: Can Platform/Runtime confirm whether metadata is intentionally dropped during route rebinds? If not, we need either:
- a short-term runtime hotfix to copy preserved client metadata into the re-attached session OR
- a recommended SDK workaround we can ship to the customer today (best would be a pin header or explicit server-side session pinning).

Longer ask (product/SDK): add a formalized client_context field the API accepts (structured JSON) that the runtime guarantees to persist across routing/failover. If we have that contract, field teams + customers can rely on it and product can own semantics.

Timeline sensitivity: Novatech is on a 2-week PoC timeline. If we can offer a mitigation within 48 hours and a roadmap commitment for an SDK + runtime contract in a sprint or two, they will continue to expand usage.

Attachments: novatech-logs-20271101.txt, repro-script-reqs.sh (small helper to reproduce), initial patch suggestion in sdk-metadata-proposal.patch (draft).

Thanks — assigning this to runtime lead to triage first pass.

— Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ashley Nguyen <ashley.novatech@novatech.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client handshake metadata gap - Novatech POC

Thanks Priyom, and thanks for the logs — that was helpful.

Quick take after an initial read: this looks like a metadata propagation gap during the connection rebind flow. When a streaming handshake is proxied and we attempt a fallback (different model variant or node), the routing layer currently re-creates a new session but only reconstructs the minimal required headers. We missed copying over arbitrary client headers (by design historically, to keep surface area small).

Short-term mitigation options we can implement:
1) Server-side copy: when a rebind occurs within the same top-level request, copy any header prefixed with x-client- or x-session- into the new session. Low-risk change, small heap impact for short-lived entries. I can scope a canaryable hotfix for this.
2) Route pin header: we can interpret an x-session-pin: true header the SDK sets to avoid rebinds for that session (this has availability/cost tradeoffs).

I need a small repro that triggers the rebind reliably (repro-script-reqs.sh may help). Please confirm the exact header names Novatech is sending (logs show x-client-id and x-call-meta). Also share the R-Trace correlation ids around the event so I can match them to our runtime traces (e.g., R-Trace: 20271101-NT-42).

Product ask: formally defining a structured client_context in the API is the correct long-term approach. If Product wants this guarantee, we need an API proposal (fields, size limits, encoding) before we ship cross-runtime persistence. I can prepare an RFC for the runtime change once we align on the fields to persist.

Proposed immediate plan: I will schedule a small canary for server-side copy (option 1) – target: EOD tomorrow for a canary deploy to a subset of nodes. If that looks good, we promote.

Karthik
Engineering Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Adding customer-impact notes from CS: Novatech has flagged ~3 demo runs where personalization keys were missing; they usually detect this in QA and roll back, but for live demos this is a showstopper. They would accept x-session-pin for now if we document the cost implications.

Product ask: Priyom's suggestion to expose a client_context JSON object makes sense for a proper contract. Suggested fields: client_id (string), customer_tenant (string), feature_flags (map of string->bool), correlation_id. Size cap: 4KB. SDKs would populate this on the create/session call and we should guarantee persistence across routing/failover.

Ops workaround for now: recommend Novatech set x-session-pin: true in their SDK and we will push the server-side copy hotfix. Also add this to the PoC runbook so Support can enable pinning if they see the pattern.

Logan

Thanks all — summary and action items below.

Summary: runtime confirms a propagation gap. Short-term server-side copy + SDK pin header are viable mitigations. Long-term: define a client_context API field with guaranteed persistence.

Action items:
- Karthik: canary server-side header copy for x-client-* and x-call-* prefixes (target: EOD tomorrow). Please post the canary rollout plan to the infra channel and include the R-Trace IDs you need.
- SDK: add an opt-in x-session-pin header + document cost/behavior in the PoC runbook (Logan/Priyom to produce wording). SDK team will also scope a client_context API addition for the next minor release (target: 2 weeks for PR). Attachments: sdk-metadata-proposal.patch is a draft we can iterate on.
- Support (cc): enable session pin on Novatech test cluster when we flip the canary; use logs in novatech-logs-20271101.txt to validate.

Customer comms: Priyom/Logan — please tell Ashley we will:
1) run a runtime canary immediately and share results in 24–36h
2) provide a documented workaround (x-session-pin) and tradeoffs
3) commit to SDK + product contract for client_context in the next minor release window

Ashley, thanks for surfacing this — we know the PoC timeline matters. We will follow up with an EOD canary report and a small runbook you can apply to your SDK while we iterate.

— Priyom

Redwood Inference
